title: Structural insights into the binding of CX-5461 and MTR-106 to G-quadruplex DNA.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed both deposited coordinate files (26JT.cif 2.0 MB, 26JR.cif 2.0 MB) from RCSB: each is one solution-NMR ensemble of 20 conformers of a single 29-nucleotide DNA (the MYT1L quadruplex-duplex hybrid, sequence AGGGAGAGGAGAGCTCTGGGTTGGGTGGG) plus one bound small molecule (ligand codes A1EOB in 26JT, A1EOV in 26JR). Titles confirm 'CX-5461-MYT1L Complex' and 'MTR-106-MYT1L Complex'. The legacy .pdb format 404s; only mmCIF exists.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The quantitative measurement table (Supplementary Table S2, melting-temperature shifts for a panel of G-quadruplex and duplex constructs with each of the two ligands) was read about only in the results text; Europe PMC's supplementary-file endpoint timed out twice, so the supplement itself was not retrievable. Row counts in Supplementary Tables S1/S2 are therefore unverified; the text names roughly 20 DNA constructs and two molar ratios.

a1_downloadable.note: Both structures download openly from RCSB with no login (verified: two mmCIF files, ~2 MB each). Chemical shifts are in BMRB 36849/36850. The NAR supplement was not retrievable via Europe PMC (endpoint timed out twice).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only numeric outcome is the melting-temperature shift on ligand binding, reported as a column in Supplementary Table S2 (read in the text, not opened). It is in a supplementary document, so it would need transcribing, but it is not constructed by inference.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are present as actual molecules: DNA sequences in Supplementary Table S1 and inside the coordinate files I opened, and the two ligands are named with CAS numbers so structures are directly obtainable.

a4_units_stated.note: Melting-temperature shifts are stated in degrees Celsius throughout the results text (for example 11.12-32.4 C for the Myc-family quadruplexes), with buffer and molar ratio given.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. Verified in the files: exactly 2 labelled complexes (one ligand each, both bound to the same 29-nucleotide DNA). The largest measurement table in the paper is roughly 20 DNA constructs x 2 ligands x 2 molar ratios, i.e. of order 40-80 melting-temperature numbers - two orders of magnitude below the ~1,500-row bar, and only 2 distinct ligands, so nothing can be held out.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; verified by downloading both files.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Matches: the deposition header records 20 submitted conformers per entry and one DNA plus one ligand, consistent with the paper's description of two solution structures.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would be physical measurements - differential scanning calorimetry melting temperatures and nuclear magnetic resonance chemical shifts - not another model's output. Provenance is fine; there is simply almost none of it.

existing_models.name: AGAPE, a machine-learning workflow that predicts whether a small molecule stabilises G-quadruplex DNA (XGBoost, a gradient-boosted tree model, on 5,666 molecular descriptors)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported ~91% classification accuracy on a curated set of 1,217 compounds labelled from FRET (fluorescence resonance energy transfer) melting assays; split details not checked
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved - only search snippets were read, not the paper

existing_models.name: G4STAB, a multi-input deep neural network predicting G-quadruplex melting temperature from sequence, salt concentration and pH
existing_models.score_and_split: R-squared about 0.8 on 2,382 DNA G-quadruplex sequences; split details not checked

existing_models.name: G4LDB 3.0, a database rather than a model - the standard training resource for this task
existing_models.score_and_split: Not a model; holds over 4,800 G-quadruplex/i-motif ligands and about 51,000 activity entries

backbone.name: ChemBERTa or MolFormer (molecular language models) for the ligand side; no backbone is useful with 2 ligands
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice, but there is nothing to fit

integration.join_key: InChIKey or CAS number of the ligand
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: A join is conceivable but pointless here: this paper adds 2 of the ~4,800 ligands G4LDB already holds, so the combined set is G4LDB.

controls.positive_control: None possible with 2 complexes; the paper's own finding (parallel quadruplexes are stabilised more than hybrid or antiparallel ones) could only be a qualitative sanity check.
controls.negative_control: Not runnable - label shuffling is meaningless at n=2 ligands.
controls.external_validation: G4LDB 3.0 and the AGAPE/G4STAB training sets exist and are far larger, which is exactly why this paper is not the dataset to start from.

honest_claim_h3: With these files a model could claim nothing: the data are two solution structures of the same DNA with two closely related ligands, so any trained model would describe two data points, not a relationship.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a small molecule's chemical structure and a DNA sequence to predict how much the molecule stabilises that folded DNA.
plain_idea.train_on: What I considered: pairs of (ligand chemical structure, G-quadruplex DNA sequence) with a measured stabilisation value. This paper supplies only about 40-80 such measurements across 2 ligands, and 2 three-dimensional structures.
plain_idea.predict: The rise in melting temperature (in degrees Celsius) when the ligand binds, measured by differential scanning calorimetry - a calorimeter that records the heat absorbed as the DNA unfolds.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Medicinal chemists designing G-quadruplex-targeted cancer drugs would use a reliable stabilisation predictor to triage compounds before synthesis; but that project needs a large ligand library such as G4LDB, not this two-ligand structural study.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper has 2 ligands and about 40-80 melting-temperature values; AGAPE trained on 1,217 compounds and G4STAB on 2,382 sequences, and G4LDB 3.0 holds ~51,000 activity entries.

confidence_score.why: No replicate spread is visible without the supplement, and with 2 ligands there is no group large enough to calibrate uncertainty on.

models_beatable.why: AGAPE (2024-2026, gradient-boosted trees on hand-made descriptors) and G4STAB (2025, sequence neural network) are both recent but descriptor-based, so a better-featurised model is conceivable - just not from this paper's data.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails on the first condition: there is no training set here to add to. The improvement would come entirely from G4LDB, making this paper irrelevant to it.

ml_idea: Rejected idea: predict ligand-induced G-quadruplex stabilisation (change in melting temperature) from ligand chemistry plus DNA sequence. The data needed for that lives in G4LDB 3.0 and the AGAPE/G4STAB training sets, not in this paper, which contributes 2 nuclear-magnetic-resonance structures of CX-5461 and MTR-106 bound to one quadruplex-duplex hybrid DNA.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the two files I actually downloaded (2.0 MB each); cross-validation time is null because no cross-validation is possible at n=2.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the labelled examples: open the two deposited structures and the melting-temperature table. 2 complexes and at most ~80 temperature values - done in ten minutes, and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: Part A5: only 2 labelled complexes exist (verified by opening both deposited coordinate files) and at most ~80 melting-temperature measurements across 2 ligands, far below any trainable size; the same task is already modelled on 1,000-2,400-compound sets.
